analysis:
Reviewed the .github/workflows/ci.yml changes: the route job now requests per-job lanes (test-provider-1..3, summary, sdk, cluster-checks, cluster-1..3, cluster-gpu-1..2, focused) via ./.github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml, and the test-provider (head 232-234), summary (477-479), sdk (675-677), cluster checks (878-880), cluster (1010-1012) jobs now use `runs-on: fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[...]`. Base text at 1053-1202 shows the non-blocking cluster GPU job and focused job with a hardcoded blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27 runner. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the head-side change for those two jobs is not visible in the supplied units (changed ranges at head 1072-1074 and 1134-1136 are the zstd echo lines, not runs-on).

Security-relevant observations: workflow permissions remain `contents: read`, and the route job has `permissions: {}`. All checkouts use persist-credentials: false and actions are SHA-pinned. Cache saves are limited to push events on master or dev (SAVE_CACHES), so PR runs cannot poison caches. The route job's outputs are used only as a runner label through fromJSON, not in shell. Lane specs interpolate only the classifier's boolean outputs, not attacker-controlled strings.

Open question outside the supplied evidence: the darkbloom-route.yml implementation is not visible. It determines whether untrusted PR code runs on Darkbloom Sandbox Macs, and whether the fallback and grant semantics are safe. The `route` job's `if: !cancelled()` runs even if the classifier fails, and the downstream jobs fall back to Blacksmith if a sandbox is unavailable. This touches TB-013 and A-019 only indirectly, since this is CI and not the provider runtime. No provider runtime, coordinator contract, or the T-041 cache code is changed. No concrete regression was identified. A reviewer of the route workflow should confirm that no secrets are exposed to sandbox runners and that PR code is isolated.
